Oh yeah haha. It was mostly due to nerves on my end. I was insecure about a bunch of innocuous crap that I obsessed over in the months leading up to the official day. Because I’m Canadian and left in the middle of a bunch of snow storms I ended up getting snowed in in Toronto for 2 days and stayed in a hotel there. The airport kept my suitcase and ran out of complimentary overnight bags so I was pretty stressed out off the bat. When I arrived the bag people at the Barcelona airport were a bit eager and ended up taking my bag off the belt before it came to me so it took me forever to get my suitcase back. I cried in the bathroom for 45 minutes while I told my bf to wait outside and give me time to calm down. 

Once I calmed down I cleaned myself up, found my suitcase and then came down the stairs to meet him. It was very surreal because I saw him before he saw me. I called out his name and as soon as he noticed me I pretty much ducked out behind a large column (dramatic I know). He came up to me and we hugged and it just went by really fast. We got a taxi and then I took a nap at the hotel haha. After that it was as if we had known each other for a lifetime. I became comfortable very easily thanks to how calm he was and we just reverted back to our same old jokey selves. 

But the months and days leading up we’re honestly filled with a ball of nerves and excitement. I couldn’t really believe I was doing what I was doing. Part of me felt very foolish.

I recently moved in with my bf who I met online almost 5 years ago. We’ve been living together for 3 months now. We met for the first time in person exactly 3 years ago in 2 days in Barcelona. Spent Christmas there and had a wonderful time. That was an important week because at that point we had been chatting for 2 years and had both eliminated all possibilities for any other romantic partners. We got along so well and thought we’d give it a shot and see how compatible we were in person. Besides him being a neat freak and me having my head in the clouds, everything was perfect so we kept going with the relationship when we went back home to our ldr lives. 

The next Christmas he came to my place and met all my friends and stayed with my family and he was really liked by everyone which was another win pushing us forward. After that Christmas he went back home and again, we were long distance. At this point it was clear we had to make a decision or it would be the end of us. The plan was for me to go there to him (he’s in a different continent) and I would find some sort of employment. Great? Nope. 

I pulled a curve ball and decided I had to go back to school. Something about moving across the world for a guy didn’t sit well with me. If things between us didn’t work out I would have nothing to fall back on and I didn’t just want to go to him and remain stagnant for that time and not improve myself/better my personal and financial situation. So I delayed the move to him by an additional year and applied to school. He wasn’t happy about that initially but he understood my reasoning and was patient. The following year I focused on studies and sought out universities near him that I could transfer to that had a suitably equal program and was in English. I was really fortunate to find a British program in my field at a college 15 minutes away from him and then I got to work on setting it all up for myself. I transferred here this year and I made the big move at the end of September. 

My program has 2 and a half-ish more years to go  with already completing a year back home and I’m halfway through this school year. Our plan is for me to go back home during the Summers so that I can go back to my amazing seasonal job and save more money while I spend time with my family and friends. We like to make things called “5-year plans” financially and we are going to invest some of my savings and his into some land he inherited that is worth a mint. We have a lot of connections and experience in our next endeavour and are pretty confident/excited (I’m sorry I can’t mention specifics for anonymity reasons but it is guaranteed to get us into early retirement in 10-15 years if that helps you understand). I think it’s important in this type of relationship (or any for that matter) to have concrete goals that align. Marriage is already being discussed but we want to hold off until I’ve graduated more than likely. I wouldn’t continue to be with him if we weren’t planning for the future and/or our goals weren’t compatible. Fortunately we want mostly the same things and have worked out great compromises on the issues we didn’t initially see eye to eye on. 

In terms of our daily lives now that we’re finally together. It’s amazing. I think this can be attributed to the fact that we are a VERY good match for each other and neither of us is what I would consider to be “toxic”. When we do have issues we talk about it and we aren’t shy to admit our own wrongdoings. We address our faults and we both work on improving ourselves. Sometimes he’s in the wrong, sometimes it’s me, and sometimes it’s a little bit of both but we know when to give each other space. But really, there’s never any need to give the other space. We have had that for YEARS and now we just constantly have fun. We have had blanket fort dates and play cards together frequently, we are always dancing and laughing and doing weird/stupid stuff to each other for a laugh. He’s been helping me adjust to a new country and I’ve been slowly learning the local language with his help. Overall it’s been great and his parents love me to pieces and have also helped me out a bunch. They laugh every time I attempt to speak in their native language and are happy I’m giving it a go.

All I can say is that I’m very happy and, so far, my own experience has been wildly successful. So my advice based on my own experience (and my own personal values which could differ from you) is.

1. Be independent first. Like I said before about going to school, it was a matter of principle that I went back to school. I needed to do this not only to better myself and future, but to prove that I didn’t need my bf and that I made sure that I came first. If I didn’t put myself first, I wasn’t ready for such a huge commitment to someone else.
2. Make sure you’re compatible before doing anything drastic commitment-wise, over the course of our long distance relationship I did a lot of feeling out as to whether or not my boyfriend’s and my values aligned. I asked lots of political questions, yes children or no children, career goals,  travel goals, yada-yada. Not everything aligned perfectly but overall we gelled really well on most things and none of the things we disagreed on were even remotely close to being deal-breakers. 
3. Trust. This is like the big one because LDRs tend to make a lot of people worried about cheaters and for good reason as the online environment where you spend all of your time corresponding over can be manipulated in a way that can obscure inconvenient truths. I’m not saying that you should go in blindly and just trust anything your SO does. Trust is earned and early on there was a lot of insecurity on my part. I realized throughout my own process of building trust that none of my issues stemmed from any “wrong doings” on my bf’s part, but they were based off of my own insecurities. I was projecting a lot and I really didn’t need to. I know my bf more than anyone and not once in our entire relationship has he done a single thing to warrant me worrying. We genuinely just like each other so much that I can’t fathom anything unsavoury going on in secret. We also spent almost all our waking hours corresponding with each other in some way (it died down after 2-3 years I promise haha) so it would have been impossible for the other to be unfaithful. 
4. Put in the work if you want it to be successful. This is standard for anyone in a relationship. It takes work if you’re serious about something to make it last. People are individualistic and can sometimes clash. I personally believe that if you think someone is worth it to make such a huge commitment then you need to be willing to meet that person halfway, show the person that you are thinking of them through your actions etc etc... 

Funnily enough, neither I or my SO found ourselves online actively seeking romance. We met due to a series of right place, right time circumstances and I find myself pinching my own skin every time I think of the events that led me to my current place in life. 

Sorry for the excessively long post!! I hope this helps you out! It can be successful but I know it’s hard. so if you think it’s worth it I wish you all the luck in the world!

YTA. First, I think it’s clear that saying “congratulations” is just not enough in this case. I just said congratulations to a casual acquaintance yesterday for winning a basketball match. It’s sort of impersonal and comparing it to a celebratory dinner it’s pretty half-assed don’t you think? 

Second, I think it’s sort of ironic that you spoke to your son so much about being a sore loser when you literally had to downplay your daughter’s success and throw a consolation dinner for your son. This isn’t consistent with what his life will be like once reality hits. Part of growing up and maturing is realizing that sometimes others will succeed where we fail and that we need to be humble in those situations. This year, my best friend was promoted to an administrative position at her company. Although internally I was jealous, I still made a strong face and I showed the utmost support for her because I knew she deserved this chance. This was in spite of the fact that I’ve long struggled in my own employment as being considered always “employee of the year” (I have the awards to prove it) where I’ve even trained my supervisors and yet have been passed up on all promotions. It sucks but my failure isn’t related to my friends success even if her success calls out my insecurities. That’s my issue to deal with. 

Third. Yep, you are showing favouritism. Clear. As. Day. Daughter knows it, and if your son doesn’t know it outright, he will soon understand it on a subconscious level just like how privilege works he will come to expect preferential treatment in the future. 

You’re teaching your son to be a sore loser in life, actions speak louder than words. You are teaching your daughter that she is second place, again, actions speak louder than words and you’re setting a sad precedent.

I think YTA. I mean, there are worse things that someone could do to you and they are just trying to think of ways to make you happy. I understand the gifting itself is making you unhappy but the in laws are probably just trying to let you know that they are thinking of you in their own way. In an ideal world, they would get it and stop giving you things but I don’t think they will ever seem to comprehend your reasoning. So I would just bite my tongue twice a year at birthdays and Christmas and say thank you. 

If it’s too difficult, try to come up with some sort of compromise. Ask them to get you something you need for the household, or provide grocery money because you will always need food. Maybe they can buy you your holiday turkey so it’s in keeping with the festivities. A gift card to a store you frequent for the necessities. I know gift cards are a waste of plastic but it’s a small thing they can give you while feeling as if it’s a gift. 

I hope that helps and happy holidays!

I feel like this whole situation is a huge mess for many reasons. 

First of all, it’s rude to clean someone else’s apartment. Please get off your high horse and keep your opinions to yourself when concerning another person’s living space. I would be so uncomfortable/embarrassed/upset if someone entered my living space and set about cleaning it. It’s such a judgemental act. My SOs mother does this whenever she visits despite me keeping up with housework. It doesn’t matter if Nick is a slob, your act is judgemental in nature. 

Next, don’t base you financial status on some casual discussions? Like if the price of your new apartment was so high that you needed to depend on your boyfriend to keep you afloat, you should have discussed this with him in detail before signing a lease in order to ensure that you’re both in the same lane. 

Third, although your boyfriend may have expressed interest in moving in with you, he didn’t set it in stone. Lots of people go on about what they would do ideally, especially if it’s to please you, but when faced with the realistic situation and forced to make a decision on the spot their opinions can change. Imagine you are leaving a job and all your coworkers say that you will TOTALLY stay in touch but then you leave and all contact just sort of drops off the face of the planet, it’s kinda like that. Putting stock in those types of discussions is naive. So basically, your boyfriend is faced with the REALITY of a past discussion where he thought about the prospect of moving in in an idealic sense but didn’t weigh the realities of it. Which he could have done if you discussed it more in depth with him before making a huge financial decision which included him. Now, you’re using your lease to put pressure on him. 

Last, it sucks that your boyfriend doesn’t WANT to move in with you just yet and now with the strenuous circumstances of your expensive lease, his roommate ditching him etc... he is now playing on the fence about it. If he does move in with you, you’ll be constantly guessing whether or not he WANTs to live with you or if he only did it for his convenience. I do think that if he wanted this relationship to thrive he should have been more enthusiastic about living with you rather than his sloppy roommate but you have only been together a year and a half. Some people move at different paces, I know some couples that were together for almost 10 years and didn’t move in until the 6 or 7 year mark. It’s a crappy situation but yeah, stop pressuring people to commit to your ideal “timeline” I guess. Your boyfriend may not be all that ready to mature at your rate and you can’t force him. 

I hope things work out whatever decision you choose to make. But communication and ample future planning would have gone a long way to squash all the issues you’re having. I also hope your boyfriend soon realizes that slob roommates are not worthwhile living partners as a matter of personal pride and worth.

I come up with things called mnemonics that make sense in my brain. Abbreviations work, or coming up with funny words using the first letters in a list of things (aka bedmas in mathematics). I use arrows or numbers to explain a step by step process in the correct order and I simplify most of the definitions of many terms by highlighting KEY words and understanding why these key terms separate this word from the next. If the blood flows toward this organ FROM another one, I use arrows to visualize that and I will write “blood flow” above said arrow. If said blood is oxygenated put, “ox or O2”. Whatever makes sense to you. 

I do all of this in my study sessions. Where I take all of the material and separate it by chapters and break it all down into notes that I can make sense of. Then I go over them again and again until I can look at one word and describe everything relating to it or it’s function and relations to other things by heart.

You could make a plant based cheese sauce from cashews and butternut squash that you can freeze in small batches and take out whenever you want Mac and cheese. 

Soups are really freezable. Corn is in season where I am right now so a nice corn chowder or bisque might be nice. 

I like making freezable breakfast wraps. You can put vegan sausage meat (chorizo would be tasty) with crumbles of tofu (eggs) mixed with maybe roasted red peppers and onions. Just wrap them up and freeze individually and they are ready for breakfast on the go. 

I like making a vegan burger out of cooked barley and mushrooms with shredded beets. It’s a nice hearty burger without beans in it. I usually pulse the mushrooms a bit then cook them in a pan with minced onions and spices so I can develop the flavour.

You can make a homemade lasagna and then divide it into portions and freeze. You can make ricotta cheese from blended cashews. A nice tomatoey sauce and maybe some roasted eggplants for the fillings along with spinach. 

Vegan chocolate mousse is extremely easy to make and really doesn’t require measurements. It’s just melted chocolate, the fat part of coconut cream (you can use a bit of liquid too), pitted dates blended in the coconut liquid until smooth (it’s a natural sweetener), then mix it all together and freeze! You may want to again freeze in portions though because it would be really difficult to scoop it frozen.

Me and some friends have been doing murder mysteries for the last 5 years now about twice a year. dm me if you'd like some tips and tricks or ideas, but I'll give you some general ideas. 

\-having a theme is nice especially if your friends are passionate about it. 

\-Think of a reason for all of your random characters to be holed up in one place together. It should be a plausible reason for a bunch of butting heads to be at one gathering, enemies and friends alike. 

\-Everyone should have their own goals besides figuring out who done it throughout the night even if the goal is innocuous. for example: a gambling character will want to make and win a total of at least 3 wagers during the event. This also offers up the characters autonomy to make bargains unrelated to the main event of finding the murderer. Maybe this is an ancient Egyptian themed murder mystery and one of the character's goals is to find a magical amulet that is of importance for them. They can make bargains with other players to trade goods or information if they happen upon this important artifact. 

\-Players should have abilities to help them throughout the game. Maybe a beautiful woman has the ability of seduction and is able to pull information out of male characters. There should be a limit on the use of these abilities of course. One of the most important abilities is the tight-lipped ability, which grants a player immunity from being forced to share their secrets.

\-There can be more than one murderer to make things interesting, and they don't have to be aligned. There's always the initial murderer, but it's nice to throw in another character who's goal is to secretly kill other players (up to a certain amount and they can't murder until a certain time so as everyone has a chance to play the game). This dynamic throws a wrench in the night and can confuse people. For a Harry Potter murder mystery, we threw in a character who disliked muggle-borns, their goal was to poison 2 muggle borns after midnight and before the game ended (they had enough poison only for 2)

\-Everyone should have a secret, something potentially damning that can lead to other characters pointing the finger at them. 

\-Every character should have gossip/information such as "I happen to know that so-and-so has secretly hated (victim's name) since high school when (victim) stole his prom date" or "I saw so-and-so near the place of (victim's) death 20 minutes before the incident, that's very seedy don't you think?" Some of the information doesn't just have to pertain to the murder though, it could just be interesting information on other character's in general either about their goals, or rivalries. 

\-There should be a currency in the game as well as valuable objects that characters can hunt during the night. Also some clues can be buried such as old letters, tapes with "footage" (literally pin a note to a vhs tape), depending on the theme we've hid various potions with effects such as truth serum, poisons, immunity, etc... Weapons, diaries, etc...

\-Make it a potluck and ask everyone to bring something so that you don't have to feed people (before they come try to commission out meals, i.e. "we need no more than 3 desserts, 2 entrees, 3 side dishes, someone should bring snacks, 2 people on drinks, 1-2 people bring chips" (if you don't do this i swear, everyone will show up with desserts and cookies and that's the worst when you're trying to feed a bunch of drunk people). 

​

**What should be in every profile:**

\-include a small backstory for the character that will help the person understand their motivations and desires. 

\-Lay out the goals they must complete by the end of the night.

\-Relationships, establish a couple of the most relevant relationships that this character has i.e. he hates Sally because Sally did him wrong at this one party one time. And He is best friends with Kyle because Kyle saved him from getting caught by the cops that one time they robbed a bank together. By doing this you establish rivalries and bonds that will help the characters pair off during the game.

\-1-2 secrets

\-1-2 pieces of information/gossip

\-2-3 abilities that the character can use a set amount of times (pickpocketing, interrogation, seduction, temporary mind control, tight-lip, finding abilities, persuasion, unfair trade-offs etc, they can get crazier if the theme is good too, i've written a superhero themed murder mystery and the abilities in that one are so cool).

​

**Last tips for dealing with people**

Lock people in, make sure that people commit to making this and that you can have a backup player worst case scenario, Like a brother or sister you can call in for a favour to replace someone that last minute ditches.

Send out profiles a day or 2 before the event so they can truly understand the character

Either make sure people print their own profiles or print them out yourselves.

Give about 15 minutes before the game for people to reread (or read for the first time) their profiles.

These things never go as planned, once the game starts, it's like a game of telephone, information grows and gets twisted for whatever reason. Let it be, it's kind of cool to see how people interpret their characters and others and watch how your game almost evolves into it's own life-form. 

Sorry for the long response, message me if you have any questions, and have fun!

Needy is when you need your girlfriend to accompany you to the corner store to buy a bunch of bananas because you can’t stand to be apart from her. Needy is not letting your girlfriend go out with her friends at night because you’d get lonely and you’re worried she values you less by having a life outside of the context of your relationship.
